vulnerabilities.title: Directory Traversal
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[ch.qos.logback:logback-classic](https://mvnrepository.com/artifact/ch.qos.logback/logback-classic) is a reliable, generic, fast and flexible logging library for Java.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Directory Traversal in `MDCBasedDiscriminator`, used by `SiftingAppender`, which takes an MDC value as the discriminating key without removing path separators, so the value reaches the nested `FileAppender` path unsanitized. An attacker can direct log output to a file outside the intended directory by supplying an MDC value containing `/` or `\` path segments. This requires a configuration whose `SiftingAppender` discriminates on MDC and whose nested `FileAppender` interpolates the discriminating key into its file path, with that MDC value populated from attacker-influenced input.

**Note:** This is a bypass of the fix for the vulnerability described in [CVE-2025-11226](https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JAVA-CHQOSLOGBACK-13169722).

## Details

A Directory Traversal attack (also known as path traversal) aims to access files and directories that are stored outside the intended folder. By manipulating files with "dot-dot-slash (../)" sequences and its variations, or by using absolute file paths, it may be possible to access arbitrary files and directories stored on file system, including application source code, configuration, and other critical system files.

Directory Traversal vulnerabilities can be generally divided into two types:

- **Information Disclosure**: Allows the attacker to gain information about the folder structure or read the contents of sensitive files on the system.

`st` is a module for serving static files on web pages, and contains a [vulnerability of this type](https://snyk.io/vuln/npm:st:20140206). In our example, we will serve files from the `public` route.

If an attacker requests the following URL from our server, it will in turn leak the sensitive private key of the root user.

```
curl http://localhost:8080/public/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/root/.ssh/id_rsa
```
**Note** `%2e` is the URL encoded version of `.` (dot).

- **Writing arbitrary files**: Allows the attacker to create or replace existing files. This type of vulnerability is also known as `Zip-Slip`. 

One way to achieve this is by using a malicious `zip` archive that holds path traversal filenames. When each filename in the zip archive gets concatenated to the target extraction folder, without validation, the final path ends up outside of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a `zip` archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicious file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```
2018-04-15 22:04:29 .....           19           19  good.txt
2018-04-15 22:04:42 .....           20           20  ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys
```

## Remediation
Upgrade `ch.qos.logback:logback-classic` to version 1.6.3 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/qos-ch/logback/commit/761821bfaacac3a0ad44fa546cfc814429bf9312)
- [Release Notes](https://logback.qos.ch/news.html#1.6.3)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Neutralization
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[net.minidev:json-smart](https://github.com/netplex/json-smart-v1) is a Java JSON parser.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Neutralization via the `parseInner` function in the `JSONParserBase` parser. An attacker can evade `JSONValue.parseStrict` or `isValidJsonStrict` by sending a valid JSON value followed by a literal `0x1A` character and malformed content; `parseInner` mistakes the character for end-of-input and skips the trailing-data check. Applications that rely on these strict-validation methods can accept input that downstream parsers such as Jackson or Gson interpret differently.
## Remediation
Upgrade `net.minidev:json-smart` to version 2.6.1 or higher.
## References
- [github.com](https://github.com/netplex/json-smart-v2/blob/v2.6.0/json-smart/src/main/java/net/minidev/json/parser/JSONParserBase.java)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/netplex/json-smart-v2/commit/e0b5afeb3bb4f5f969c233c60e9aeca0a6338d7e)
- [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/netplex/json-smart-v2/issues/302)
- [GitHub PR](https://github.com/netplex/json-smart-v2/pull/305)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2556274)
- [Vulnerable Code](https://github.com/netplex/json-smart-v2/blob/ebf7cf8cf0dccef246cd1ed0d052074d787a2de4/json-smart/src/main/java/net/minidev/json/parser/JSONParserBase.java#L229-L240)

vulnerabilities.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in the `createParserFactory` and `createDocumentBuilderFactory` methods of the `XmlFactory` class, which set only `XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING` on the factory and leave `disallow-doctype-decl`, `external-general-entities`, `external-parameter-entities`, and `load-external-dtd` at their defaults. An attacker can read local files out of band by submitting XML containing an external entity declaration to an application that unmarshals untrusted documents. Exploitation depends on the JAXP implementation in use, because secure processing alone does not block external entity resolution on every implementation.

## Details
XXE Injection is a type of attack against an application that parses XML input.
XML is a markup language that defines a set of rules for encoding documents in a format that is both human-readable and machine-readable. By default, many XML processors allow specification of an external entity, a URI that is dereferenced and evaluated during XML processing. When an XML document is being parsed, the parser can make a request and include the content at the specified URI inside of the XML document.

Attacks can include disclosing local files, which may contain sensitive data such as passwords or private user data, using file: schemes or relative paths in the system identifier.

For example, below is a sample XML document, containing an XML element- username.

```
<xml>
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>
   <username>John</username>
</xml>
```

An external XML entity - `xxe`, is defined using a system identifier and present within a DOCTYPE header. These entities can access local or remote content. For example the below code contains an external XML entity that would fetch the content of  `/etc/passwd` and display it to the user rendered by `username`.

```
<xml>
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [
   <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd" >]>
   <username>&xxe;</username>
</xml>
```

Other XXE Injection attacks can access local resources that may not stop returning data, possibly impacting application availability and leading to Denial of Service.

## Remediation
A fix was pushed into the `master` branch but not yet published.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/jaxb-ri/commit/abf8c9707046d78bd3b7e834596feb3d3c21dbcb)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/jaxb-ri/commit/c08fde59)
- [GitHub PR](https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/jaxb-ri/pull/2013)
- [GitLab Work Item](https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/cve-assignment/-/work_items/310)

vulnerabilities.title: Symbolic Name not Mapping to Correct Object
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Symbolic Name not Mapping to Correct Object through the `getInstantiatorOf` process. An attacker can cause objects from one class loader to be substituted into another by exploiting instantiator caching keyed on class name, potentially leading to unexpected behavior, data corruption, or application crashes by introducing wrong-class objects.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.objenesis:objenesis` to version 3.6 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/easymock/objenesis/security/advisories/GHSA-743r-26gf-97ff)
- [github.com](https://github.com/easymock/objenesis)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/easymock/objenesis/commit/40f90f435a06b16af74a7398f0007faeaa52c00c)
- [Vulnerable Code](https://github.com/easymock/objenesis/blob/fb36e5c377ed1bf57a18386fa79d2eed4ddfcfac/main/src/main/java/org/objenesis/ObjenesisBase.java#L92-L95)

vulnerabilities.title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity via the `computeAllFrames` method in `MethodWriter`. An attacker can exhaust CPU and tie up class-file transformation threads for an unbounded time by supplying crafted class files for processing with `ClassWriter.COMPUTE_FRAMES`; their methods make frame computation’s fixpoint algorithm converge slowly.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.
## References
- [GitLab Commit](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/commit/ab68bbd2521359b7c8cd3517c6331ced3d817ed0)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/blob/ASM_9_10_1/asm/src/main/java/org/objectweb/asm/MethodWriter.java#L1595)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/merge_requests/463)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2552253)

vulnerabilities.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value via `readBootstrapMethodsAttribute()` in `ClassReader`. When an application parses an attacker-supplied class file, a crafted BootstrapMethods attribute with an unchecked declared length can trigger an allocation of roughly 2 GB from a file of about 100 bytes, causing an `OutOfMemoryError` that crashes the JVM or the thread processing the class.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.
## References
- [GitLab Commit](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/commit/eb5fa95bb0670eaec2ecf9b8a3a501b48e5a967c)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/blob/ASM_9_10_1/asm/src/main/java/org/objectweb/asm/ClassReader.java#L3497)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/merge_requests/456)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2552305)

vulnerabilities.title: Uncontrolled Recursion
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Recursion via the `parseType` method in `SignatureReader`. An attacker can trigger a `StackOverflowError` and disrupt class transformation by supplying a crafted class file with a `Signature` attribute containing deeply nested generic type arguments.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.
## References

- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/merge_requests/465)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2552264)

vulnerabilities.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value via the `addSubroutineRetSuccessors()` method in the `Label` class. An attacker can crash the JVM by supplying a crafted invalid class file with multiple `RET` instructions for one `JSR` while ASM processes the subroutine.

**Notes**

- The attacker must get a user to load or process the crafted class file.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.
## References
- [GitLab Commit](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/commit/4dabfe0aef14f8cccb0617640a4add8fbcc4ed36)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/blob/ASM_9_10_1/asm/src/main/java/org/objectweb/asm/Label.java#L568)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/merge_requests/458)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2552308)

vulnerabilities.title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity via the `computeAllFrames()` and `computeMaxStackAndLocal()` methods in `MethodWriter`. When ASM processes a crafted class file with thousands of overlapping exception handlers using `COMPUTE_FRAMES` or `COMPUTE_MAXS`, it allocates excessive `Edge` objects, causing an `OutOfMemoryError` that crashes the JVM.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.
## References
- [GitLab Commit](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/commit/91057c98239d994aed5e46434e34e00d593c0daf)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/blob/ASM_9_10_1/asm/src/main/java/org/objectweb/asm/MethodWriter.java#L1662)
- [gitlab.ow2.org](https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/-/merge_requests/461)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2552285)

unresolved.title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
unresolved.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity via the `computeAllFrames` method in `MethodWriter`. An attacker can exhaust CPU and tie up class-file transformation threads for an unbounded time by supplying crafted class files for processing with `ClassWriter.COMPUTE_FRAMES`; their methods make frame computation’s fixpoint algorithm converge slowly.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.

unresolved.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
unresolved.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value via `readBootstrapMethodsAttribute()` in `ClassReader`. When an application parses an attacker-supplied class file, a crafted BootstrapMethods attribute with an unchecked declared length can trigger an allocation of roughly 2 GB from a file of about 100 bytes, causing an `OutOfMemoryError` that crashes the JVM or the thread processing the class.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.

unresolved.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value via the `addSubroutineRetSuccessors()` method in the `Label` class. An attacker can crash the JVM by supplying a crafted invalid class file with multiple `RET` instructions for one `JSR` while ASM processes the subroutine.

**Notes**

- The attacker must get a user to load or process the crafted class file.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.

unresolved.title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
unresolved.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity via the `computeAllFrames()` and `computeMaxStackAndLocal()` methods in `MethodWriter`. When ASM processes a crafted class file with thousands of overlapping exception handlers using `COMPUTE_FRAMES` or `COMPUTE_MAXS`, it allocates excessive `Edge` objects, causing an `OutOfMemoryError` that crashes the JVM.
## Remediation
Upgrade `org.ow2.asm:asm` to version 9.11 or higher.
